precepts.text: Whoever will not receive you, shake off the very dust from your feet and wash your hands of them.
precepts.point: Give not that which is holy unto the dogs nor cast your pearls before swine: there is no magic scripture, you cannot save everyone, and some are predestined to be stupid.

note.label: Untruthful Trinity Revisited & Ridiculous

precepts.why:
“Give not that which is holy unto the dogs, neither cast ye your pearls before swine, lest they trample them under their feet, and turn again and rend you.” Don't waste your time talking to dumbass people; they'll turn against you and fight you. There is no magic scripture. You cannot save everyone. Some people are meant, predestined, to be stupid.

Luke gives the instruction Christ gave: “And whosoever will not receive you, when ye go out of that city, shake off the very dust from your feet for a testimony against them.” Shake off the very dust. Wash your hands of them and leave them alone.

If you explain that the heavenly Father is the Most High God, that he has a son, and that his son has sons, the children of Israel, and they can't understand it and say no, they're all one, leave that negro alone. You're wasting your time; he is on medications or should be.

The proverbs read with it say the same: “If a wise man contendeth with a foolish man, whether he rage or laugh, there is no rest.” There is no conclusion; it is a circular argument that goes nowhere. “The heart of the foolish is like a cartwheel; and his thoughts are like a rolling axletree.” Three is one, one is three, round and round. These are unreasonable people, so you shake off the dust and move on.

precepts.text: No man, having put his hand to the plough, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God. That's a hireling. Some of y'all sitting here right now. There is a God; remember that.
precepts.point: So this is where you self-examine: am I being a phony, a hypocrite amongst the brethren? Am I walking feignedly? Only you can answer that. You and God know the answer; we don't. If a sister ask us, what about this brother, we can only tell her what you show us. Is he really like that? You got to talk to this guy more in depth, more personally, to find out how they truly are. And some brothers can fake it real good.

note.label: Living Your Life As A Hireling

precepts.why:
“And Jesus said unto him, No man, having put his hand to the plough, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God.” That's a hireling: he put his hand to the work and then looked back. Some of y'all are sitting here right now. There is a God; remember that.

This is where you self-examine. Am I being a phony, a hypocrite among the brethren? Am I walking feignedly? Only you can answer that. You and God know the answer; we don't.

Ezra prays that God would think not upon those that walked feignedly, but remember them that have known his fear. The one who looks back from the plough is not fit for the kingdom.

precepts.text: No man, having put his hand to the plough, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God. When you turn back, regardless of your great speech, you have taken your hand off the plow. You can try to manipulate his words to justify it all you want.
precepts.point: And when he could not overcome Onias, he got him to Apollonius the governor of Coelosyria and Phenice. He ran to the other nations. They were working together on this temple, and because of one argument he goes to the other nations against Onias, and told them that the treasury in Jerusalem was full of infinite sums of money. You cannot make this stuff up.

note.label: From Brother To Betrayer

precepts.why:
Simon of the tribe of Benjamin was the governor of the temple, working alongside Onias. When he “fell out with the high priest” and “could not overcome Onias”, he turned back and ran to the nations. Christ says of that: “No man, having put his hand to the plough, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God.”

You put your hand to the plow to do the work. Then you get frustrated with brothers always correcting you because you are doing stupid stuff, and now you are mad, you are going to separate yourself and do your own thing. Simple.

Brothers and sisters, when you turn back, regardless of your great speech, we're still keeping the commandments, you have looked back. You have taken your hand off the plow, and Christ said you are not fit for the kingdom of God. You can try to manipulate his words all you want to justify it, but that is what Christ said.

precepts.text: He spake of the kingdom of God and healed them that had need of healing: Christ is the only one who can heal us.
precepts.point: Therefore all they that devour thee shall be devoured and all thine adversaries, every one of them, shall go into captivity, Miss Laura included, and all that prey upon thee shall be a prey. For I will restore health unto thee: only the Lord heals, by Christ's stripes, for they that are whole need no physician and he came to call sinners to repentance. Because they call thee an outcast, African-American, Haitian, Jamaican, this is Zion whom no man seeketh after.

note.label: From Exile & Tribulation to Promise

precepts.why:
“For I will restore health unto thee, and I will heal thee of thy wounds, saith the Lord”. The Lord is the only one who can restore health; that goes back to verses 12 and 13, “thou hast no healing medicines.” There is no magic voting right and no economic situation to save us.

Luke shows who the healer is: “And the people, when they knew it, followed him: and he received them, and spake unto them of the kingdom of God, and healed them that had need of healing.” Christ spake of the kingdom and healed them that had need of healing. He is the only one who can heal us of all these things. He is the Saviour; he is the physician.

That is how the incurable bruise of Jeremiah 30 is cured. Not by any medicine of man, but by the Lord who received the people, taught them the kingdom of God, and healed them.

precepts.text: When the Samaritans would not receive Christ, James and John wanted to call down fire as Elijah did, and he rebuked them: ye know not what manner of spirit ye are of. Know what spirit to be in with people in the street, and sisters too, because brothers do the work and sisters undo it by not saying shalom when the people come in. Represent this truth with professionalism; map out whom you can reach the moment you enter a room. You do not have to be a soldier: an 83-year-old brother in New York hands out fifty flyers a week and got his home health aide wearing dresses. Be fishers of men, because war is imminent.
precepts.point: His God doth instruct him to discretion. Discreet means careful and circumspect in speech or action, to avoid causing offence or to gain an advantage. Learn discernment: how to speak and when to speak, which someone should tell our wives, in order to win souls.

note.label: America At War With Iran: Preparation For Conflict

precepts.why:
The fitches are not threshed with a threshing instrument, nor the cummin under a cart wheel; each seed has its own instrument. Even the disciples used the wrong one. The Samaritans “did not receive him, because his face was as though he would go to Jerusalem. And when his disciples James and John saw this, they said, Lord, wilt thou that we command fire to come down from heaven, and consume them, even as Elias did?” Let's go get the death scriptures; let's pray the Lord takes them out.

“But he turned, and rebuked them, and said, Ye know not what manner of spirit ye are of.” Brothers, you have to know what manner of spirit you're supposed to be in when you deal with the people in the street. Sisters, the same way. Sometimes the brothers do the work, the people come in, and the sisters undo the work by not saying hello, shalom, or Christ bless. Sisters need to learn how to fish too.

Always represent this truth with the utmost professionalism, because we have a job: to win souls, and we don't have much time. As soon as you step into a room or a store, map out whom you think you can bring the truth to. You don't have to be a soldier to do that. Brother O'Shea in New York is 83; he hands out his fifty flyers a week, and the home health aide who came to him from the nursing home started wearing dresses.

We must be fishers of men, because war is imminent and danger is coming. Knowing the right spirit for each person is the discretion God instructs the plowman in.

precepts.text: If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily.
precepts.point: Deny yourself, take up your cross daily, and follow Christ.

note.label: Kill Or Be Killed

precepts.why:
“I protest by your rejoicing which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord, I die daily.” What did Paul do? He died daily. Paul put himself out there, did the work, and killed the old man daily. Brothers, that is your job too: you have to kill that old man daily.

But how do you do that? Did Paul just sit on his ass? Christ makes it very clear: “And he said to them all, If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me.” That is how he dies daily: he denies himself, and he takes up his cross.

We are all commanded to take up our cross and die daily. To take up your cross is to accept your death when it comes. Kill the old man. And if they take you out, take your death: we will be back.

It is a war. You have to execute the man in you to be able to see the conniving, deceitful, envious, jealous, hateful, murderous spirit of these other nations against our people. You have to remove that old man to have a sense of clarity. Twelve tribes, twelve trials.

precepts.text: John forbade one casting out devils in Christ's name because he followed not with them, and Christ said, Forbid him not, for he that is not against us is for us.
precepts.point: The same is a lesson today: do not envy the gift on another brother or sister, but glean from it. A brother may be a better teacher, a sister a better labourer; go and learn from them rather than rolling in envy, for the Lord would put His spirit upon them all.

note.label: Numbers 11: Beware of Murmuring

precepts.why:
Joshua the son of Nun said, “My lord Moses, forbid them”, when Eldad and Medad prophesied in the camp. Moses answered, “Enviest thou for my sake? would God that all the Lord’s people were prophets, and that the Lord would put his spirit upon them!” Joshua was carrying a spirit of envy, and Moses corrected it.

The apostles had the same spirit. “And John answered and said, Master, we saw one casting out devils in thy name; and we forbad him, because he followeth not with us. And Jesus said unto him, Forbid him not: for he that is not against us is for us.” John wanted to forbid a man because he was not in their company, as Joshua wanted to forbid the two in the camp; Christ answered like Moses did.

The Most High wants all His people to be prophets. The lesson today is the same: do not envy the gift on another brother or sister, but glean from it. A brother may be a better teacher, a sister a better labourer; go and learn from them rather than rolling in envy, for the Lord would put His spirit upon them all.

precepts.text: When the Samaritans would not receive Him, James and John wanted to call down fire; Christ rebuked them, Ye know not what manner of spirit ye are of, for the Son of man is not come to destroy men's lives, but to save them.
precepts.point: The same is a lesson today: do not envy the gift on another brother or sister, but glean from it. A brother may be a better teacher, a sister a better labourer; go and learn from them rather than rolling in envy, for the Lord would put His spirit upon them all.

note.label: Numbers 11: Beware of Murmuring

precepts.why:
Moses asked Joshua, “Enviest thou for my sake?” Joshua did not know what spirit he was speaking from, and neither did James and John.

When Christ sent messengers into a village of the Samaritans and “they did not receive him, because his face was as though he would go to Jerusalem”, James and John said, “Lord, wilt thou that we command fire to come down from heaven, and consume them, even as Elias did? But he turned, and rebuked them, and said, Ye know not what manner of spirit ye are of. For the Son of man is not come to destroy men’s lives, but to save them.”

Christ rebuked the wrong spirit in His disciples as Moses rebuked the envy in his young man. The man of God corrects the spirit, and the Lord's people are to be prophets, not enviers.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 20

precepts.why: “Let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me”: that requires one word, discipline. Could have, should have, would have: that is Satan. You could have been all that, but the things you would have had to do are where the sin begins. “For whosoever will save his life shall lose it”: losing your life doesn’t mean suicide; it means losing the path you were gunning for, and following Christ. “For what is a man advantaged, if he gain the whole world, and lose himself, or be cast away?” Satan offered Christ all the kingdoms of the world if he would worship him, and he says the same to us. “There be some standing here, which shall not taste of death, till they see the kingdom of God”: they died and are gone, so they are coming back, and when the Lord returns they will see him with their own eyes and meet their ultimate death and damnation. There are levels in this book.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 1 A Visit From The Lord

precepts.why:
“For whosoever shall be ashamed of me and of my words, of him shall the Son of man be ashamed, when he shall come in his own glory, and in his Father’s, and of the holy angels.”

“But I tell you of a truth, there be some standing here, which shall not taste of death, till they see the kingdom of God.” That is a heavy verse right there. There be some standing here which shall not taste of death till they see the kingdom of God, meaning when they see them chariots coming.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 2 Message to the 7 Churches

precepts.why: “For whosoever shall be ashamed of me and of my words, of him shall the Son of man be ashamed”. Christ comes in his glory, his Father's glory and that of the holy angels. Do not be ashamed of what the Bible actually says. Holding his name and refusing to deny the faith means standing by his words when they are unpopular or dangerous.

note.label: Daily Bread for a Dying Man

points: And Jesus said unto him, No man, having put his hand to the plough, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God. You cannot do what you want to do; you have to do it the right way, straight.

An officer opened up the agriculture in it: plowing is the first step; you plow, then you sow, then you harvest, then you replenish. When people stop doing the work, they get disenchanted with the things they did first. The scripture says remember thy first love, and hold the beginning of your confidence stedfast unto the end. Do not get disenchanted with the things you did when you first came in; go back to that first love, because when you lose the plowing, you cannot do the other prerequisites to harvest.

A Rochester officer spoke on preparation: a lot of the Bible is agriculture related, because that was our culture back then; we had our own, and we are going to have our own again. If you do not know how to self sustain, learn it; there are skills out there. Get the body together, unify, be communal, so that those serious about the walk can be fed and sought for in that day. The Lord said he has never seen the righteous forsaken, nor his seed begging bread; when the grinding is low, as prophecy says, it is the local congregation's job to be self sufficient for the people. That is what love is.
